newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam's rice market in Tet lull.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam's rice market in Tet lull.

text.p: Vietnam's export rice market was very quiet on Wednesday as much of the country remained off work following the Tet lunar new year holiday.

Dealers in Ho Chi Minh City said prices were unchanged from their levels before the start of the holiday a week ago at around $270 per tonne FOB Saigon Port for five percent broken grade and $260 per tonne for 10 percent broken.
But with trade just resuming only a few thousand tonnes were reported sold.
Dealers said rumours of a possible rice deal with the Philippines involving the purchase of more than 100,000 tonnes of local rice remained widespread.
Talk of the deal initially surfaced last month, but traders said they now expected a Vietnamese government delegation to head to Manila later this week, or early next, to discuss the deal.
Vietnam's domestic media reported on Wednesday that Hanoi was hoping for record exports of up to 3.5 million tonnes of rice this year.

The Saigon Times Daily said an initial quota of 2.5 million tonnes had been set for the period from January to September, with a further one million tonnes likely after that, assuming no major damage to crops from annual flooding.
Vietnam exported more than three million tonnes last year making it the world's third largest rice exporter after Thailand and the United States.
